    "text": "nd lipoprotein(a) in men and women\n\nAssociation of cholesteryl ester transfer protein genotypes with CETP mass and activity, lipid levels, and coronary risk\n\nABCA1 and ABCG1 or ABCG4 act sequentially to remove cellular cholesterol and generate cholesterol-rich HDL\n\nEvaluation of Isis Apo(a)Rx, an antisense inhibitor to apolipoprotein(a) in healthy volunteers\n\nMipomersen, an apolipoprotein B synthesis inhibitor, lowers low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in high-risk statin-intolerant patients: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial\n\nA first-in-man, randomized, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the safety and feasibility of autologous delipidated high-density lipoprotein plasma infusions in patients with acute coronary syndrome\n\nMCP-1 binds to oxidized LDL and is carried by lipoprotein(a) in human plasma\n\nDiscrete roles of apoA-I and apoE in the biogenesis of HDL species: lessons learned from gene transfer studies in different mouse models\n\nA new recombinant human apolipoprotein E mimetic peptide with high-density lipoprotein binding and function enhancing activity\n\nPleiotropic effects of statins: basic research and clinical perspectives\n\nApheresis\n\na procedure used to remove a substance from blood circulation. Whole blood is drawn from the body by large catheter and separated into different blood components. The desired substance can then be removed, with reinfusion of remaining blood products to the body.\n\nAtherosclerosis\n\nthe process of cholesterol plaque deposition and inflammation along arterial walls. It can result in obstruction to blood flow and a tendency to thrombosis with sudden vessel occlusion.\n\nChylomicrons\n\nlarge lipoprotein particle that carries dietary lipid and is rich in triglyceride.\n\nFoam cells\n\nmacrophages or immune cells containing excess cholesterol, largely due to uptake of oxidized LDL.\n\nHigh-density lipoprotein (HDL)\n\nApoA1-containing lipoprotein; major function is reverse transport from peripheral sites to liver for excretion.\n\nIntermediate density lipoprotein\n\nformed by action of lipases on very low-density lipoproteins, resulting in increased cholesterol and decreased triglyceride content and smaller size, compared with VLDL.\n\nLipoprotein\n\nparticles consisting of surface proteins and phospholipid and a neutral lipid core, functioning to transport of lipids throughout the circulation.\n\nLow-density lipoprotein (LDL)\n\nApoB-containing lipoprotein. Major carrier of cholesterol esters to peripheral cells.\n\nMyopathy\n\nmuscle disease that in general describes muscle weakness or pain.\n\nHepatic steatosis\n\ncaused by an imbalance of lipid uptake or synthesis compared with clearance from the liver.\n\nVery low-density lipoprotein\n\ncarries triglycerides and cholesterol from liver to peripheral tissue and contains apolipoproteins B, C, and E."
  },
